739 millionyouth and adults worldwide still lack basic literacy skills; about 63% are women.2026 reporting based on UNESCO data
Access gapDevices, reliable internet and digital knowledge remain unevenly available.
Guidance gapSkills alone are not enough; learners also need relevant, personal mentorship.
01Our mission

Bridge the divide with useful learning.

Useful learning changes what feels possible. DigiPath is an online mentorship and learning initiative designed for underprivileged youth, connecting foundational knowledge to digital confidence, stronger decisions and career opportunity.

01

Build the learning platform

Create an accessible digital home for guided learning, mentorship and skill development.

02

Grow career readiness

Help learners build practical knowledge they can carry into education, work and everyday life.

03

Strengthen the ecosystem

Bring learners, mentors, volunteers and NGO partners together around the same path.

02Learning tracks

Five skills that open doors.

Every track is free for early learners during launch. Choose one place to begin or take the complete pathway.

01

Conversational English

Build practical speaking, listening and everyday communication confidence.

Free for early learners
02

Basic Math

Strengthen numeracy, problem-solving and the calculations used in daily life.

Free for early learners
03

Digital Literacy

Learn to use digital tools with confidence, judgment and online safety awareness.

Free for early learners
04

Financial Literacy

Understand budgeting, saving, responsible spending and simple financial choices.

Free for early learners
05

Health Literacy

Make sense of everyday health information and practice informed self-care.

Free for early learners

The complete DigiPath

Follow all five tracks as one connected path—from core confidence to real-world readiness.

Best starting point · Free during launch
03Mentorship

Guidance that grows with the learner.

Personalized AI guidance can support a learner now. The longer-term direction is a trusted human network built with NGO and volunteer partners.

Available in the concept

AI-based one-to-one guidance

Personalized learning paths can respond to pace, progress and the skills each learner wants to build.

→
Roadmap

Human mentors through partners

Volunteer and NGO collaborations are intended to add encouragement, context and real-world career perspective.

Partner discussions, mentor onboarding and progress-tracking tools are still in development.
04How it works

A practical path, one step at a time.

DigiPath is designed around movement—not passive content. Each stage turns knowledge into confidence and readiness.

1

Learn

Start with clear, accessible lessons in a chosen track.

2

Practice

Apply ideas through everyday examples and small exercises.

3

Get mentored

Use personalized guidance to stay moving and solve gaps.

4

Get career-ready

Carry practical confidence into education and work.

05Shared direction

Learning with wider impact.

DigiPath’s mission aligns with three United Nations Sustainable Development Goals identified in the original initiative plan.

04

Quality Education

Accessible learning and skills that support lifelong opportunity.

08

Decent Work

Foundational and digital skills that strengthen career readiness.

10

Reduced Inequalities

More equitable access to knowledge, guidance and digital confidence.

Expected outcomesMore confident digital participation, stronger everyday decision-making, clearer learning pathways and improved readiness for future education and work. These are intended outcomes; measured impact will be published as programs and tracking mature.

07Questions

What to know before you begin.

Launch details are clear about what is available now and what is still on the roadmap.

The initiative is designed for underprivileged youth who want stronger foundational, digital and career-readiness skills.

Every learning track is free during launch for early learners. Future paid plans are not active.

Regional-language expansion is on the roadmap. The launch language list has not yet been finalized.

Human-mentor and NGO partnerships are in the discussion phase. A formal onboarding channel will be added as those partnerships are finalized.
